National Weather Service Fort Worth TX
547 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
 
- Patchy, occasionally dense, fog is expected overnight into
  Thursday morning across much of the region.

- Tranquil weather with above-normal temperatures are forecast
  through Saturday.

- A cold front will bring bring very low rain chances (10-20%) 
  Saturday night or early Sunday along with cooler temperatures 
  that linger into next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(This evening through Thursday)
Issued at 1253 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

A tranquil midweek is expected across the region as upper-level 
ridging remains the key player in the weather pattern through the 
end of the week. A weak shortwave disturbance will continue 
transiting through the Plains this afternoon into tomorrow, but 
will remain weak and displaced enough to preclude any impact. 
Mostly sunny skies and east-southeasterly winds will aid in 
warming temperatures into the 60s and 70s today. Winds will once 
again become light overnight tonight, setting the stage for 
patchy, sometimes dense, fog across much of the region prior to 
the influx of upper-level cloud cover tomorrow morning. Visibility
reductions are likely during the morning commute, so make sure to
check road conditions and give yourself plenty of time to get to 
your destination if your location is impacted by fog. Tomorrow 
will have a bit more cloud cover, but southeasterly winds will 
still keep temperatures in the mid 60s to mid 70s.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Thursday night through next Tuesday)
Issued at 1253 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

The end of the week is expected to be quiet, with south-southeast
winds continuing to pump warm and moist air across Texas. Heading
into the weekend and into next week, a bit of a more active 
pattern is anticipated as longwave troughing will set up across 
the western CONUS. Multiple shortwaves are expected to round the 
base of the trough and eject through the Plains over the long term
period. The first of which will occur Saturday into Sunday. This 
shortwave will shunt a cold front south through the region later 
in the day. There remains uncertainty on whether or not any rain 
will accompany this front, and will really depend on the track of 
the shortwave. The GFS is the wetter deterministic solution with a
more southerly track, and the ECMWF is drier and more northerly. 
The NBM seems to lean more towards the Euro as rain chances have 
diminished. Further strengthening confidence in a drier FROPA, 
just under 30% of total ensemble members are outputting the 
southerly, wetter solution.

Outside of any rain chances, the front will usher in a period of 
much cooler conditions, with afternoon highs in the 50s and 60s 
and lows in the 30s and 40s to kick off next week.

An additional shortwave will eject across the Plains midweek next
week, with the potential for scattered rain chances returning to 
portions of the region on top of another intrusion of cold air. 
Midweek highs in the 50s and lows in the 30s and 40s are 
anticipated. The active pattern looks to continue the rest of the 
week with groups of GEFS/EFS members hinting at periods of rain, 
but deterministic guidance diverges significantly on time and 
place and the overall pattern this far out. Make sure to keep 
updated with the forecast as we go through the rest of this week 
into the weekend, as more details will become available once mid-
range (and eventually high-resolution and short-range) models 
start to come into play.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 545 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

VFR will continue this evening as a ridge remains positioned
overhead. A departing shortwave in the Plains, light winds, and
clear skies will then create good radiative cooling conditions
overnight. Some visibility reductions will become possible by
daybreak Thursday as temperatures fall into the upper 40s/lower
50s and dewpoint depressions approach zero. The better fog
potential will be in rural areas of North and Central Texas, but
will maintain a TEMPO for MVFR visibility 11-15Z at all airports
where at least minor drops in vis are still expected. Whatever 
the case, will need to monitor METAR and satellite trends tonight.
Conditions will return to VFR late Thursday morning.
